rounds.text: Atul Auto Ltd (ATULAUTO) appears to be under-appreciated based on the evidence provided. The company's compounded profit growth over the last five years is a staggering 47%, which significantly outpaces its share price increase of only 9%. This strong fundamental performance, as indicated by [E19], suggests that ATULAUTO could be undervalued relative to its peers and current market expectations. The positive screen reasons such as sales growth [E64], strong sales growth [E65], and multi-year sales uptrend [E67] further support this view, indicating that ATULAUTO may be outperforming its peers in terms of revenue generation. Moreover, the company's discounted cash flow (DCF) analysis suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 704 per share against a market price of Rs 386, leaving a margin of safety of 45.1%. This DCF valuation [E45] implies that ATULAUTO is trading at a significant discount to its true worth based on future cash flows. While the stock's P/E ratio (23.4) and P/B ratio (2.19) are slightly above sector benchmarks, these metrics do not necessarily indicate underperformance since they reflect the company's strong fundamentals. The recent profit growth of 47% CAGR over the last five years [E60] is a positive indicator that ATULAUTO has been outperforming its peers and market expectations. In conclusion, the evidence supports an argument for ATULAUTO being undervalued based on its robust profit growth and strong fundamentals. The intrinsic value derived from DCF analysis suggests that investors could benefit from holding this stock within the current price range.

[E19] (bull) Compounded profit growth over 5 years is 47%. [E20] (bull) Compounded profit growth over 3 years is 125%. [E21] (bull) Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months is 69%. These three points strongly imply that Atul Auto Ltd has been experiencing strong and consistent earnings growth. The compounded profit growth over five years, three years, and even in the most recent period of the trailing twelve months all exceed 50%. This level of sustained profitability suggests a solid foundation for the company's valuation. However, it is important to note that these figures are not supported by the P/E ratio [E6] which stands at 22.42x against a sector benchmark of 21.66x. This discrepancy implies that the market may be undervaluing Atul Auto Ltd based on its earnings growth potential, as it is trading below the sector average despite strong profit growth. [E5] (bear) The stock sits 9% of the way up its 52-week range (366 low to 597 high). This indicates that the current price may be overvalued relative to historical performance. While this alone does not necessarily mean the company is undervalued, it suggests that investors might be paying a premium for growth potential. [E40] (neutral) CWIP stands at Rs 7 Cr (Sep 2026), a +133.3% move on the prior year. [E45] (bull) A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 704 per share against a market price of Rs 386. These points suggest that Atul Auto Ltd has significant capital expenditure plans, which could lead to future growth and justify its current valuation. [E47] (bull) A reverse DCF says today's price already implies 9.8% earnings growth, against the 18.0% the base case assumes. This further supports the notion that Atul Auto Ltd is undervalued based on its recent performance and future expectations. In conclusion, while there are some discrepancies in valuation metrics such as P/E ratios, the strong compounded profit growth over multiple periods strongly implies that Atul Auto Ltd carries significant value. The sector median profit growth [E74] (bull) at 23.0% also supports this view, suggesting that the company is performing well relative to its peers. Conceded: [E1] (bull), as a P/E of 23.4x does not necessarily imply overvaluation if it aligns with strong earnings growth and market conditions.
